clue.text: Commander's recording uranium in vapour clouds in space

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for Commanding Officer, so a commander's gives CO plus S

indicators.note: the recording and the uranium sit inside the word for vapour

parts.note: mist is a fine watery vapour
a CD, compact disc, is a recording
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A commander's tape captures radioactive vapour drifting among the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine particles of matter drifting between stars form clouds of this material.

clue.text: Horn succeeded in competition for trophy

indicators.note: the abbreviation for succeeded is placed within the contest word

parts.note: a cup is a competition played for a trophy
s. is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A horn player triumphed in a contest for a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A cusp is a pointed end, like the horn of a crescent moon.

clue.text: Page bound with more out-of-date office equipment

indicators.note: the page letter is held within the comparative word, as if tied up inside it

parts.note: staler means older and less fresh

explanation.surface: A page tied up with yet more dated office kit.
explanation.definitionFit: This device fastens sheets of paper with wire clips, a standard piece of desk gear.

clue.text: Concerned with defences, colonial mum worried about American soldier

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the soldier abbreviation
worried suggests the letters of colonial and mum are fretted into a new order

parts.note: GI is the standard term for an American soldier

explanation.surface: A colonial mother frets over a visiting American serviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective relates to the study of the body's immune defences against disease.

clue.text: Staff upped and established a southern county

indicators.note: in a down clue upped means the staff word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
set means fixed or established

explanation.surface: Workers lifted their game and founded something in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upped' turns ROD into DOR. DORSET is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a county on the south coast of England, a straightforward example of the class.

clue.text: Crush emptied into rather large glass

indicators.note: the remaining letters go inside the word for rather

parts.note: sooner means rather, as in I'd sooner not

indicators.note: emptied means the inside of crush is removed, leaving its outside letters

explanation.surface: A crush of people poured into a fairly big glass.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tall glass for sherry or beer, larger than a standard measure.

clue.text: Unmatched son's chances

parts.note: odd describes a sock or glove that has no match
s is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: An odd-one-out son's prospects are being weighed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting odds express the likelihood or chances of something happening.

clue.text: Thomas was one man of action, but quaking on the inside

indicators.note: the shaken letters are placed within the man of action

parts.note: a doer is someone who acts rather than talks

indicators.note: quaking suggests the letters of but are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Thomas was a decisive man outwardly, but trembling within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quaking' makes UBT. The definition alludes to 'doubting Thomas', the apostle who would not believe in the Resurrection until he saw the wounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Thomas would not believe until he saw, making him the classic sceptic.

clue.text: Be agitated about women's skill in love

indicators.note: the agitation word goes round the women abbreviation

parts.note: to seethe is to be agitated or inwardly furious
w is the abbreviation for women
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: Getting worked up over a woman's talent for romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is an endearment for a dear one, just like this word for a beloved.

clue.text: Prison's fierce critic

definitions.meaning: someone who slams things, criticising them harshly

explanation.definitionFit: Both a slang word for jail and someone who harshly attacks things in reviews.

clue.text: It's hairy when their suffering holds us back

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hold the turned pair inside them
suffering suggests the letters of their are put through distress into a new arrangement
back means the word us is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A hairy situation when their pain keeps us from moving on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' makes HIRTE and 'back' makes SU. 'It's ... when' is surface padding around the one-word definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal synonym, describing a body covered in a lot of hair.

clue.text: Combined acting job, having directed also in pub in it

indicators.note: the directed and pub pieces go inside the acting job word

parts.note: a role is a part, an actor's job
led means guided or directed

indicators.note: the word for also sits inside the pub word

parts.note: an inn is a pub
too means also

explanation.surface: An actor landed a role and directed it, also running a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for several things merged together into a single whole.

clue.text: After high temperatures, you'll have a sudden dip here

definitions.text: After high temperatures, you'll have a sudden dip here

parts.words: After high temperatures, you'll have a sudden dip here
parts.note: the surface sounds like a weather forecast of a cold snap, but describes the cold bath you jump into after a sauna

explanation.definitionFit: A small cold pool beside a sauna, which bathers plunge into after the heat.

clue.text: Child not transformed in Looking- Glass?

indicators.note: a word unchanged in a mirror reads the same backwards and forwards, with a nod to Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A youngster in Carroll's story who stays the same through the mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small child, an informal everyday synonym.

clue.text: Bishops are not constrained by the rank and file here

definitions.text: Bishops are not constrained by the rank and file here

parts.words: Bishops are not constrained by the rank and file here
parts.note: sounds like church politics, but rank and file are rows and columns, and chess bishops move diagonally across them

explanation.definitionFit: The chequered playing surface where bishops move diagonally through ranks and files.

clue.text: Barrier in road left blocking shade

indicators.note: the road and left letters block the shade word by sitting inside it

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A barrier in the road on the left is blocking the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurdle is a fence or obstacle that must be jumped over.

clue.text: Train in connection with last ride, perhaps

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a hearse carries a coffin on its final journey

explanation.surface: A train linked to someone's final journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Train here is a verb meaning to practise or prepare by repetition.

clue.text: Poet's curious name to catch when it comes up

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the whole string is read bottom to top

parts.note: nosy means inquisitive or curious
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: A poet's peculiar name gets caught as it rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when it comes up' turns the whole of NOSYNNET round. Alfred, Lord Tennyson was Victoria's Poet Laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Tennyson was a Victorian Poet Laureate, so he is an example of a poet.

clue.text: Runner's more pleased with himself when crossing line?

indicators.note: the comparative word crosses, that is goes round, the line letter

parts.note: smugger means more self-satisfied

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied athlete crossing the finishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' and 'line' suggest athletics; a runner here carries contraband, and the line is the border.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner is someone who runs goods illegally, as in gunrunner or rum-runner.

clue.text: Sportsman's partner in nude, abandoned without an income

indicators.note: the partner word is placed within the shuffled letters
abandoned suggests the letters of nude are let loose in a new order

parts.note: WAG, from wives and girlfriends, is British slang for a footballer's partner

explanation.surface: A footballer's partner in the nude and abandoned, without a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' makes UNED. WAGs (wives and girlfriends) is British tabloid slang for the partners of footballers.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwaged describes those with no paid job and so no earnings.

clue.text: Handle that turns opener round back of tin

indicators.note: the comparative word goes round the final letter

parts.note: wider means more open

indicators.note: back of means the final letter of tin

explanation.surface: A can opener's handle turns round the back of the tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' looks like a tin opener but means 'more open', WIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A winder is a crank or knob you turn to wind something.

clue.text: Furry animals found in frigid sleeping quarters?

parts.note: a dorm is a dormitory where people sleep
ice stands for something frigid, icy cold

explanation.surface: Furry creatures discovered in a freezing bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Small furry rodents known for long hibernation, so these are animals.

clue.text: End of lifeline in upturned hand attached to arm

indicators.note: the last letter goes inside the turned hand word
in a down clue upturned means the hand word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a paw is an informal word for a hand

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of lifeline

parts.note: on means attached to, as in a lid on a jar

explanation.surface: A palm reader studies the end of the lifeline on an upturned hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upturned' turns PAW into WAP, and 'in' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Arm as a noun is a weapon, as in firearms.

clue.text: Old actress's acknowledgment of applause

definitions.meaning: Clara ... was a star of silent films
performers bend forward at the waist when the audience claps

explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the silent screen's It girl and the gesture of thanks at a curtain call.

clue.text: Something supposed to summon, restricting European court

indicators.note: the summoning word restricts the European court pair by enclosing it

parts.note: to conjure is to summon up, as a spirit

explanation.surface: Summoning someone while restricting the European court seems a supposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A guess or supposition, something put forward without proof.

clue.text: Judge the weight of man standing on foot

indicators.note: in a down clue the man word stands on top of the foot abbreviation

parts.note: he refers to a man

explanation.surface: Gauge how heavy a man is by having him stand on someone's foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something to estimate how heavy it is.

clue.text: Bell from a set kept in student union

indicators.note: the set word is kept inside the union abbreviation

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students in Britain
gel means set, as jelly does

explanation.surface: A bell taken from a set stored in the students' union building.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angelus is a Catholic devotion announced by the ringing of a bell, and the bell itself.

clue.text: Outline condition rejected among working class

indicators.note: the turned word sits among the letters of the working class word

parts.note: prole, from proletarian, is a working-class person

indicators.note: rejected means the condition word is sent back and read in reverse

parts.note: if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: The state of things outlined, rejected by the working classes.
explanation.definitionFit: A profile is a side outline of a face, or a sketch.

clue.text: I'm among Carroll's characters those corresponding to Carl, in his real name

definitions.text: I'm among Carroll's characters those corresponding to Carl, in his real name

parts.words: I'm among Carroll's characters those corresponding to Carl, in his real name
parts.note: the extinct bird in Alice in Wonderland stands for Carroll himself, whose real name Dodgson was said to come out stammered

explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll was Charles Lutwidge Dodgson; Carroll comes from Carolus, i.e. Charles (Carl), and his stammered surname supposedly gave the bird its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird in Alice's adventures is Carroll's self-portrait, based on his own surname.

clue.text: Foolish to let off steam over end of play, whatever happens

indicators.note: the foolish word goes over the last letter, enclosing it

parts.note: inane means silly or foolish

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of play

parts.note: to vent is to release pent-up feelings

explanation.surface: Foolish to blow your top at the close of the show, whatever happens.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning regardless, whatever the outcome may be.
